title.narrative: Output 6.4. Increased capacity of Member States to strengthen legislation, polices and measures to ensure equal opportunities and treatment in the world of work for persons with disabilities and other persons in vulnerable situations

description.narrative: 1. In 2022, through support from the ILO/EU Spotlight Initiative an Action Plan for the Inclusion of Persons With Disabilities(PWDs) in workplace Policies and Programmes on Violence and Harassment at Work was adopted by government and social partners in 2022. 2. An HIV/AIDS Combination Prevention and Gender Based Violence(GBV) Programme Targeting Young Workers in the Mining Sector was developed and implemented jointly with the National Aids Council(NAC) for enhanced life skills, sexuality education, condom use, voluntary medical male circumcision, access to Sexual Reproductive Health(SRH) services, and reduce vulnerabilities and exposure to GBV. a. The programme has reached 665 workers with HIV prevention and behaviour change information and strategies; over 9,000 male condoms and 1,600 female condoms were distributed. 342 workers accessed HIV Testing Services(HTS) and 42 peer educators were trained. 3. In 2022, forty(40) Labour Inspectors were sensitised on key ILO tools to promote workplace non-discrimination and inclusion including the ILO Convention No. 190; ILO Recommendations No. 200 and No. 206; and the Handbook on HIV and AIDS for Labour Inspectors in line with the national instruments (Code of Good Practice on HIV and AIDS and the World of Work). 1. The ILO provided technical and financial for the conducting of a study on inclusion of PWDs in workplace policies and programmes on ending violence and harassment at work. a. As part of the Action Plan fifty(50) Gender Champions were also sensitised on C190 and R206 for policy and workplace programme design and implementation. 2. The ILO with support from the Unified Budget, Results and Accountability Framework (UBRAF) engaged the Zimbabwe AIDS Prevention and Support Organisation (ZAPSO) to design and implement the programme for young workers. The ILO provided technical inputs on the mainstreaming of the ILO instruments.

Output 6.3. Increased capacity of Member States to develop gender-responsive legislation, policies and measures for a world of work free from violence and harassment

description.narrative:
1. In 2023, the Government of Zimbabwe gazetted a new Labour Amendment that provides for definition of Gender-Based Violence and Violence and harassment in line with C190 and R206. 2. In addition, to strengthen the capacity of all actors in the world of work and ensure the application in practice of Convention No. 190, the Government, in consultation with the social partners, developed and adopted a Training Manual for Policy Development and Programme Implementation Addressing Gender Based Violence and Sexual Harassment in the Workplace. The Training Manual is meant to guide tripartite plus constituents in developing and implementing policies and Model Workplace Programmes (MWPs) to end violence and harassment in line with C190 and R206 at enterprise, sectoral and national levels. 3. Over the period 2022-2023 and with support from the EU funded Spotlight Initiative (SI) fourteen (14) private sector companies have developed and are implementing workplace policies and Model Workplace Programmes (MWPs) to end violence and harassment. The programmes have targeted over 10,000 workers in the hospitality, wholesale and retail, financial services, telecommunications, manufacturing, and public services.
4. Workers and Employers' Organisations conducted bipartite advocacy campaigns with Parliamentarians for ratification and application of C190 and R206 in law and practice. 1. The ILO supported sensitisation activities for key stakeholders including workers and employers' organisations on C190 & R206. The social partners then held policy advocacy interactions with Parliamentarians including the Parliamentary Committee on Employment and Labour. The ILO provided texts of the Convention and Recommendation to support the engagement on the Labour Amendment by Parliament, the Senate and CABINET. 2. The ILO conducted awareness raising activities on C190 and R206 for management and shop floor staff reaching over 10,000 workers. Technical and financial support was extended for the drafting of policies, training of Workplace Committees and Gender Champions to promote the policies and workplace programmes.

Output 6.2. Increased capacity of Member States to strengthen policies and strategies to promote and ensure equal opportunities, participation and treatment between women and men, including equal remuneration for work of equal value

description.narrative: In August 2023, the Government of Zimbabwe gazetted an amendment to the Labour Act (Chapter 28:01) -Labour Amendment No. 11 that revises provisions in the Act that promote substantive equality between women and men in the world of work: a. The Labour Amendment No. 11 amends Section 5 of the Act by the repealing section 2a and substitutes it with a new provision that provides for equal remuneration for work which is of equal value: ‘Every Employers shall pay equal remuneration to male and female employees for work to which equal value is attributed without discrimination on the grounds of sex and gender'. Over the period 2022-2023 the ILO provided technical support to the Ministry of Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare and the Attorney General’s Office during the drafting of the amendment on the interpretation of the principle of equal pay: a. In this respect, the ILO shared information relating to the concepts underlying this principle, which is at the heart of the ILO's Equal Remuneration Convention, 1951 (No. 100) and insights on how it can be applied in practice as outlined in the Equal Pay - An introductory guide. b. The ILO NORMES Department provided detailed technical comments on the draft Labour Amendment Bill in June 2022 as a follow-up to discussions during the ILO Direct Contacts Mission (DCM) in April 2022. The Direct Contacts Mission was recomended by the Committee on the Application of Standards (CAS) of the International Labour Conference at its 108th Session (June 2019) with respect to the application of the Freedom of Association and Protection of the Right to Organise Convention, 1948 (No. 87) and the of the 2009 Commission of Inquiry’s recommendations. One of the recommendations of the CAS was to amend the Labour Act, in consultation with workers’ and employers’ organizations. c. The ILO also facilitated the development of a position on the Labour Amendment Bill by the Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions which was shared with the ILO Direct Contacts Mission and Government
